reviews.title: Misleading membership and refusal of Refund
reviews.text: I downloaded the app without any clear indication that this was a membership and an annual fee. I did not give a credit card but was still charged, presumably through my Apple account. They claim 48 hour grace period to cancel but only in store credit and still charging me $99.99.  Referring to terms and conditions to keep 100$ is a very poor business model.

reviews.title: Zero chance
reviews.text: You have to give a form of payment before viewing anything on the app. No payment terms are disclosed. Within 15 minutes of signing up, I had received 4 marketing emails. Deleted immediately. Do not fall for this.

reviews.title: Scam warning: Do not download if you are just browsing!
reviews.text:
Do not download this app if you are just browsing. They will charge you $99.99 without disclosing it anywhere upfront. When you try to look into it, they try to cover it up by claiming it’s just a $1 authorization charge that will be refunded.
On top of the deceptive billing practices, their customer support is absolutely horrible. I have sent multiple emails over the past two weeks trying to get my money back and haven’t received a single response. Avoid this company unless you want your money taken and your emails ignored.

Whatever you do, don’t sign up for this

reviews.title: Deceptive Practices
reviews.text: The company puts a case drop out there and if you select the wine, they sign you up.  I don’t want to be a member.  I am already a member of NakedWines, a terrific company.  Sad!!

reviews.title: Nonsense
reviews.text: You can only buy from the wines listed on their drop. You can't actually shop for what you want. Terrible service.

reviews.title: Rip Off
reviews.text: $25 for shipping doesn’t save you anything. App charges you the second you select a bottle to add to basket then you can’t remove it. I had to reactivate to ship bottles bc I couldn’t get it off credit card. Too many suspect things with this app

reviews.title: Scam and Fraud
reviews.text: You cannot view the wine options without giving access to either Apple Pay or credit card. It says there is no cost, but you are actually signing up for a $99 membership. There is no notification or warning that this is happening. In addition, despite providing an option to change privacy settings, the provided links do nothing other than “reset“ any previous settings. Given how scammy the app is, I can only presume that this negates any privacy settings you may have previously selected. Lastly, over the last 30 minutes I have received no less than three app notification and four texts.

reviews.title: Almost a Scam. Stay away
reviews.text: App is pretty much a scam. Almost sure these reviews are all fake. First, it asks you for Apple Pay for a free subscription, doesn’t not tell you that you have 3 days to cancel it, or you will be charged $100 for the annual membership. You have to go on their website to cancel it, luckily I did it in time. Also, I was just trying to figure out the app, added one the wines to the CART, it did not show anything or showed something saying that I would be charged, but since it had my Apple Pay information, it charged for the bottle right away. Tried to contact costumer service, no response. It’d be nice if it wasn’t tried to scam you every second and I’d have probably purchased a case.

reviews.title: Very Misleading
reviews.text: Like many others have said on their own reviews this app is very misleading. Went through the process to explore the app and see what it was like and when I came to the subscription services I exited the app and deleted it without choosing a subscription or acknowledging to start the free trial. I was charged 100$ for a yearly subscription and upon seeing this not even 8 hours later I cancelled my forced membership but am told it’s in place for the duration of the time. This site is very misleading in which it forces you into a membership. Make sure you don’t put in a payment method unless you are sure this is what you want. Also since I now have the subscription for a whole year I decided to check out the app and am very disappointed in the extreme lack of items. I logged on and only have a choice of one bottle of wine, no other choices and no way to search bottles. This app is for the birds and I highly suggest anybody who is considering this to move on to something else.

reviews.title: Horrible user interface
reviews.text: First of all I was just wanting to check this app out to see what it was like. I didn’t realize it would charge me the full membership fee after I literally deleted the app. I didn’t want to enroll in their membership. Then they would only give me Store credit so I was like fine. I’ll just buy some wine with the Store credit even though I already was upset cause I didn’t want Store credit. I just wanted my refund from the membership. I ordered wine and I didn’t realize that the button that says by now you would think oh I guess that means by now, but I just read it more as you added it to your shopping cart and you’re not charged immediately at that second and then I was charged for the bottles I added to my shopping cart cause that’s how I viewed it the top with the interface makes it look so I bought literally the same wine twice when I did not mean to the user experience is horrible is not intuitive. It is so confusing. I am very unhappy.

reviews.title: Beware: Deceitful Subscription Practices and Zero Customer Care
reviews.text:
I strongly advise anyone considering CaseDrops to think twice before signing up.

Their subscription practices feel incredibly predatory. The way the membership is presented makes it far too easy to be charged for recurring payments without a clear understanding of what you’re agreeing to. Many customers don’t realize they’re enrolled until they see charges on their credit card, and when they contact support, they’re met with little to no willingness to make things right.

What was most disappointing was the refusal to issue a refund, even after explaining the situation. Instead of valuing long-term customer trust, they hide behind their terms and conditions while keeping money from customers who clearly didn’t intend to continue the subscription. Just because something is buried in the fine print doesn’t make it good customer service.

A reputable company should prioritize transparency, send clear renewal reminders, and work with customers when honest mistakes happen. Instead, CaseDrops appears to profit from confusion and then refuses to take responsibility when customers ask for help.

There are plenty of companies that earn repeat business through great products and honest customer service. In my experience, CaseDrops has done the opposite. I won’t be purchasing from them again, and I would caution others to read every detail before providing payment information.

reviews.title: Be careful!
reviews.text:
I literally downloaded the app and watched the video to understand how it works but because it’s linked to my Apple ID account it automatically meant that I signed up for the three day trial and then was just billed the $70. I absolutely did not click on the link that said I wanted to have a trial membership because as soon as I saw that there was a yearly membership fee. I did nothing else, but the app was on my phone and automatically linked to my payment information. I am so frustrated that every company is using this type of marketing ploy to dupe people into paying even a one time additional fee of now $70 when I had no intention of using it. I am a tech savvy person. I was truly just curious and did not click on something saying yes I want to have a trial membership.

The best was: they say there is a grace period if you change your mind within the first 48 hours after billing so in my case, I should be eligible for a refund. They said yes, you’re eligible for a refund, but that refund, as it turns out, is issued in the form of a store credit. So they still keep your $70 and I guess hope that you spend it but it’s also unclear because it says it’s only valid through the end of the billing period but as my account is canceled, what does that mean the 48 hours?

reviews.title: Waste of money
reviews.text: First you can’t set up and account and take a look. They say they aren’t billing you today but once you click in your enrolled and a payment plan is set up. Membership can be canceled but our still on the hook for a year. Selection is minimal and they are probably just here for the fees. You also can’t remove your card even after you cancel so that data is always there sitting. Which in today’s world of breaches is not good for the consumer.

reviews.title: Credit info immediately?
reviews.text: The last thing I want to do is add a payment method as one of the absolute first things I do when I try to download or sign into a brand new app. If you absolutely need my payment information before I can open up your app and search the deals, then that is a dealbreaker…. I mean that is equal to someone calling me and the first thing they want is my credit card information before they will talk any further…. Absolutely asinine.!

reviews.title: Money taken without my consent
reviews.text: Either a scam or very deceptive app. I downloaded this on Monday the 30th March as I was curious. As soon as I saw it had a subscription model, I deleted it. I have since been charged 69.99$ with NO email confirmation of purchase and there is no subscription active in my Apple account. Either a scam or terrible, deceptive UI.

reviews.title: AI Slop app
reviews.text:
AI slop app forcing you to set up a membership before you can even view anything on the application.  If you signed up via Apple, it’s impossible to then cancel your account/ membership because they require that memberships must be cancelled on their website, but if you try to sign up in via Apple it sends you straight back to the app. Garbage stuff. 

Oh and the silly video by the CEO at the start with no option to skip definitely is why I decided to cancel and delete my account

reviews.title: SCAM WARNING: Deceptive Ads and Unauthorized Charges
reviews.text:
Avoid this app at all costs! They are using blatant 'dark patterns' and deceptive advertising on Instagram to trick users. I clicked on an ad showing impossible prices for premium champagne, only to find out the app is a front for a forced subscription.
The most alarming part is that they started charging my account without my explicit consent. I never authorized a trial or a subscription plan, yet the charges appeared immediately. This is a predatory business practice and a total scam. I have already reported this to the App Store and my bank. Do not download CaseDrops unless you want unauthorized charges on your card!

reviews.title: Misleading interface
reviews.text: This app starts off by forcing you to subscribe to some membership before explaining the benefits or allowing us to see how the app works. The selection was extremely limited, and I would not have proceeded if I knew that there were only 4 bottles on offer at a time. I suggest revising the app to allow customers to experience the interface and see the selection first. Then, after they decide they want to purchase a bottle, you can commit them to the membership. Seems very sketchy and misleading, and I have immediately cancelled my subscription and deleted the app!
